title: 2026 年假日 Live-Ops：节庆活动的设计支柱
content:
'Tis the Season: Holiday Live-Ops in 2026
Skip to content
Weekly Digest
‘Tis the Season: Holiday Live-Ops in 2026
By Tim Shepherd •   September 27, 2026
Winterfest 2025 promotional artwork | Source:
Epic Games
Fundamental design pillars of in-game events include novel content, exclusive rewards, and a time limit. A national holiday supplies all three wrapped in real-world festivities, which is why seasonal content such as Halloween, Christmas, and Valentine’s Day became the backbone of OG live-ops long before events ran constantly. As we head into the annual run of big events, we wanted to take a look at how seasonal live-ops perform in 2026.
Live-ops doesn’t take days off anymore. Most top mobile games now run major seasonal events as one entry in a constant stream of quests, tournaments, and sales, not as the rare interruption it used to be. Over
90% of the top 100 grossing U.S. iOS games run seasonal events
, and the number of live-ops events per game climbed from
73 to 89 per month over the course of 2025 alone
. If every week already has an event, what does dressing one of them up for Christmas add? We pulled a decade of Sensor Tower revenue and download data across 14 top mobile titles, plus console and Roblox data, to find out.
Mobile games analyzed:
Candy Crush Saga,

All Trick, No Treat?
Halloween week revenue lift by market, 2024–2025 medians | Source: Naavik,
Sensor Tower
Across our mobile cohort, median revenue during Halloween week runs from 0.97x to just 1.05x that of a normal week in every market we checked, from the U.S. to Korea, and has since 2016. Battle Royale is an outlier: PUBG Mobile Global’s Halloween week has run a median 1.22x to 1.38x since 2022 (as high as 1.90x in 2024), and the lift has held every year since 2018. Gruesome time-limited skins and unique zombie modes are on brand for both the game and the holiday.
Merge Mansion — like most leading titles — provides weeks of Halloween-themed content each year | Source:
Pocket Gamer, Metacore
Console shows a similar pattern. Call of Duty’s annual Halloween event, The Haunting, has run since 2020, and Fortnitemares has run every year since 2018. When a game leans thematically or mechanically into Halloween territory, the uptick seems more substantial.
Fortnitemares reveal 2026 | Source:
Fortnite
Of course, most games run some form of Halloween events and promotions. Teams keep running them because players expect them, and that expectation is worth meeting even when revenue doesn’t move much.
Meta’s own developer guidance is blunt about this
: players “have learned to anticipate that major changes will align with holidays,” and a game that skips the moment risks losing them to one that doesn’t. The anticipation shows up in player sentiment regardless of what the revenue data says: outlets from
YouTube
to
Vice
cover Fortnitemares leaks every year.
Black Friday Isn’t About the Game
Call of Duty Mobile Black Friday promotion | Source:
Activision
Black Friday works differently from Halloween because it doesn’t ask players to “feel” festive about the game. Instead, it imports a discount habit players already have from shopping everywhere else at that time. Our mobile cohort’s median lift has held at around 1.19x for ten straight years. And it travels: the same lift shows up in Japan (1.50x), Germany (1.27x), and Korea (1.12x), markets where Halloween barely registers.
Black Friday week revenue lift by market, 2024–2025 medians | Source: Naavik,
Sensor Tower
Arguably, Black Friday is very much a U.S. tradition, but a good deal is rarely questioned!
About 30% of casual mobile titles now
offer Black Friday sales globally. For example, Coin Master runs Black Friday harder than most, driving close to 1.9x normal weekly revenue two years running.
All I Want for Christmas Is Robux
Christmas revenue lift used to be much more significant to our cohort than it is now. Five of our sample titles have run a Christmas event every year for a decade: Candy Crush Saga, Clash of Clans, Coin Master, Monster Strike, and Pokémon GO. Their combined median Christmas-week revenue lift fell from 1.88x that of a normal week in 2017 to 1.01x in 2025.
Christmas-week revenue lift, 2017–2025: Clash of Clans vs. the 5-title cohort median | Source: Naavik,
Sensor Tower
Clash of Clans shows it most clearly: from 2.6x normal weekly revenue in 2017 down to 0.85x in 2025 (though this followed a particularly strong November for Clash of Clans, alongside an overall increase in live-ops activity across titles in recent years).
Christmas 2025, U.S.: downloads lift vs. revenue lift | Source: Naavik,
Sensor Tower
Christmas largely delivers new players, not just more spending from existing ones. Cohort downloads jump 1.41x in Christmas week while revenue sits at 1.05x, matching Sensor Tower’s long-standing attribution of December’s revenue lift to
new devices, first-time users, and gift-card credit
rather than any in-game event. People naturally have more time to play and check out more games.
When it comes to younger audiences,
nearly half of U.S. kids surveyed this year said in-game currency — specifically V-Bucks and Robux — was what they wanted for Christmas
. In other words, they want gift cards, not to spend time responding to mobile in-game banners.
GTA Online Christmas 2025 | Source:
Rockstar
Converting seasonal traffic into revenue depends on providing compelling purchasing opportunities when players arrive and introducing impactful progression gates shortly after download. Last War and Whiteout Survival also generate 1.3x to 1.5x baseline revenue through Christmas week because their genre is more suited to aggressive monetization and hard progression gates. Those arrive within the first few days of install, so a December cohort converts while
